purpose: Persistent, model-independent record of interesting patterns, model consequences, null-model outcomes, and research priorities. Entries are hypotheses-to-test or simulation consequences unless explicitly backed by observation.

status_vocabulary.PATTERN_WATCH: Statistically or structurally interesting; requires stronger controls or data.
status_vocabulary.MODEL_CONSEQUENCE: Follows from stated assumptions; not an observation.
status_vocabulary.NEGATIVE_RESULT: A tested pattern did not survive controls.
status_vocabulary.CONFIRMED_OBSERVATION: Reserved for directly supported observational evidence; simulation alone cannot assign this.
status_vocabulary.SOURCE_CONFLICT: Two source locations or versions disagree; preserve both until scope/error is resolved.
status_vocabulary.SYNTHESIS_BASELINE: Cross-source explanatory baseline supported by the current corpus; not recovered ancient testimony and not geometry truth.

invariants: A finding never changes geometry provenance or evidence maturity by itself.
Simulation-only findings must say SIMULATED or MODEL_CONSEQUENCE.
Pattern significance must record its null/control family.
Missing uncertainty is never treated as zero.
Every release reviews existing findings for supersession, strengthening, weakening, or closure.

entries.title: Conditional deep gravity signature is shaft-dominated
entries.summary: In the current conditional deep geometry, the shaft-only map peaks near 251.96 µGal while the terminal-only map peaks near 31.75 µGal. The modeled near-surface shaft geometry dominates the peak surface signature.
entries.why_interesting: If the literal shaft geometry existed, a gravity survey should be designed around the near-surface column signature rather than only the deep terminal volumes.
entries.next_test: Use site-realistic topography, geological density heterogeneity, instrument noise and survey geometry before detectability claims.
entries.guard: Conditional model consequence only; not evidence that the shafts exist.

entries.title: Known-interior acoustic mode coincidences remain a pattern watch
entries.summary: The known/derived interior produced 7 near-coincidence clusters. It lies near the 97th percentile of the independent ±5% null and 91th percentile of the construction-aware null.
entries.why_interesting: The signal weakens under a more realistic null that preserves repeated construction relationships, so it is worth tracking but does not establish deliberate tuning.
entries.next_test: Add gabled geometry, measured loss parameters, coupled-volume FEM and in-situ impulse-response data.
entries.guard: Pattern watch, not tuning evidence.

entries.title: Deep conditional geometry enters a high-overburden regime
entries.summary: The vertical overburden proxy is 16.52 MPa at 648 m and 18.36 MPa at 720 m. The Khafre backing-limestone sample UCS prior is 12.1–17.8 MPa.
entries.why_interesting: The simple load proxy overlaps or exceeds the sample-scale UCS range, making rock-mass structure, joints, confinement, support and excavation history first-order requirements for any literal deep-cavity interpretation.
entries.next_test: Build a rock-mass model with stratigraphy, discontinuities, horizontal stress, water state and cavity-shape stress concentration; then run mesh-converged FEA.
entries.guard: rho·g·h / UCS ratios are not factors of safety and cannot prove impossibility.

entries.title: A connected deep water column would carry multi-MPa pressure
entries.summary: If a fresh-water column were hydraulically connected to 648 m depth, static pressure would be about 6.35 MPa and gravitational potential about 1.77 kWh/m³. At 720 m the static pressure would be about 7.06 MPa.
entries.why_interesting: Hydraulic claims become quantitatively demanding at these depths, but pressure head alone says nothing about actual water, recharge, permeability, flow rate or extractable power.
entries.next_test: Acquire groundwater level, permeability, fracture/connectivity and boundary-head evidence before any flow model.
entries.guard: Conditional hydrostatic consequence only; GIZA currently has no evidence of a connected water column.

entries.title: Flow rate is intentionally unresolved
entries.summary: STRATA refuses to compute a flow rate because permeability, connectivity, recharge/discharge boundaries and hydraulic gradients are unresolved.
entries.why_interesting: This prevents hydrostatic head from being misrepresented as evidence of a functioning hydraulic system.
entries.next_test: Populate permeability/connectivity/head-boundary evidence with provenance before enabling Darcy-flow calculations.
entries.guard: Unknown inputs remain unknown rather than receiving convenient defaults.

entries.title: Modern Khafre surface survey is the highest-value evidence gap
entries.summary: AERA publicly lists a 2025 first laser survey of Khafre, while GIZA still lacks the underlying measurements/point cloud. Public GPMP/Dash survey-control resources now provide a concrete registration path for exterior imagery, but no modern Khafre laser values are ingested.
entries.why_interesting: This is the cleanest path to reducing exterior geometry uncertainty without relying on speculative physics.
controls: Do not infer unpublished laser values
Preserve Petrie as historical backbone until modern data are actually acquired and registered
Require CRS/scale/uncertainty/rights metadata before geometry promotion
entries.next_test: Acquire authorized Khafre laser-survey data or published derived measurements plus Dash/GPMP control files; register CRS/datum and compare residuals against Petrie/M&R before any geometry promotion.
entries.guard: Publication existence is not measurement access. No laser-derived geometry was invented or promoted.

entries.title: Khafre tensile minimum has a source-internal discrepancy
entries.summary: The Heritage Science prose reports a Khafre/Chephren split-tensile range of 1.79–3.71 MPa, while Table 13 sample 5 reports 1.49 MPa. REGISTER preserves both rather than normalizing the conflict away.
entries.why_interesting: A 0.30 MPa change at the low end is material to weak-rock screening and demonstrates why sample rows are safer than broad prose summaries for solver priors.
controls: same-paper paragraph vs Table 13 row audit
entries.next_test: Verify the published PDF/table typesetting and any corrigendum; retain sample 5 = 1.49 MPa unless primary-source correction establishes otherwise.
entries.guard: This is a source audit, not a new laboratory measurement and not a monument-wide material property.

entries.title: SAR Doppler tomography method lineage is retracted
entries.summary: Remote Sensing retracted the 2022 SAR Doppler tomography pyramid paper on 10 August 2026 after its investigation reported serious methodological flaws and statistical errors that undermined the paper’s scientific conclusions.
entries.why_interesting: Any Khafre hidden-structure narrative relying on the same method lineage needs independent raw-data validation and non-retracted replication before it can influence geometry.
entries.next_test: Seek independent raw data, independent method validation, peer-reviewed Khafre-specific results, or orthogonal sensing such as muography/survey data.
entries.guard: Retraction of a method paper does not directly disprove every separate claim; it removes GIZA’s basis for treating that method as validated evidence.

entries.title: Open historical + modern imagery can become a registered condition time series
entries.summary: Khafre now has a registered open-media discovery surface spanning Commons pyramid/interior/detail/historical/temple categories plus 406 Digital Giza photo records. A 2016 open-access condition study reports facade photography from 2009–2012 with in-situ crack verification in 2012.
entries.why_interesting: Once images are camera/plan registered with residuals, repeated viewpoints may support condition-change, casing, fracture and surface-state studies without relying on memory or visual impression alone.
controls: no metric inference from uncalibrated single views
entries.next_test: Run desktop Commons harvester, cache license-eligible originals with hashes, select repeat-view pairs, solve camera pose/control against survey geometry, and quantify registration residuals before extracting measurements.
entries.guard: Open-image abundance is not evidence of new structures and is not metric geometry until calibration/control passes.

entries.title: Khafre photo registration can be anchored to public survey-control resources
entries.summary: The open-media atlas now has a defensible bridge toward spatial registration: AERA documents the GPMP survey-control network, while the Dash survey index identifies public Giza corner/center and GPMP control datasets. REGISTRATION LAB seeds camera priors and world-control candidates but does not claim any photo pose is solved yet.
entries.why_interesting: This replaces “align it until it looks right” with a residual-audited route from photographs to survey-referenced spatial evidence.
controls: native survey CRS/datum retained until transform receipt
no geometry write before VAULT/FIELD review
entries.next_test: Acquire Giza-Corner-Points-2v17.kmz and GPMP-Control-Monuments.kmz, register their coordinate frame, download eligible photo originals, mark pixel correspondences, and solve the first exterior camera poses with holdout residuals.
entries.guard: No camera pose or metric geometry has been inferred from metadata alone.

entries.title: Khafre casing foundation is measurably counterclockwise from true cardinality
entries.summary: The 2006 Total Station survey gives casing-foundation DFCs of -3.8′ north, -4.0′ east, -5.8′ south and -4.2′ west. A common-yaw least-squares summary is -4.45′ (-0.07417°), with 0.792′ RMS side residual and 2.0′ total side spread across 54 measured points.
entries.why_interesting: This is the first survey-derived Khafre angular control in the GIZA registration stack and can constrain exterior photo registration without pretending the pyramid is an exact square.
controls: retain side residuals instead of averaging them away
reported 0.2′ repeatability treated as repeatability, not total uncertainty
entries.next_test: Acquire/parse Khafre survey control coordinates and mark real exterior image correspondences; test whether survey-constrained camera solutions agree on held-out points.
entries.guard: This confirms a surveyed casing-foundation orientation pattern only. It does not prove every masonry course shares the same yaw and does not establish GPMP translation or elevation.

entries.title: Survey orientation is ready, but real camera poses remain correctly blocked
entries.summary: CONTROL NET can now supply a measured Khafre orientation prior and published GPMP frame/control context, but all real registration jobs still have zero marked pixel correspondences and zero promoted camera poses.
entries.why_interesting: The remaining bottleneck is now concrete: acquire/hash the control assets, solve the survey-to-local translation, and mark real image controls rather than adding more schema or aligning photos by eye.
controls: real jobs stay unsolved without pixel controls
projective DLT benchmark is synthetic only
consumer photo GPS remains context only
translation receipt required for GPMP-to-local use
entries.next_test: Cache the corner/control KMZ assets, parse Khafre/GPMP controls, issue the first horizontal transform receipt, then solve one exterior photo with fit and independent holdout residuals.
entries.guard: No real camera pose or photo-derived metric geometry has been promoted.

entries.title: Public GPMP controls provide a concrete bridge from historical survey to modern registration
entries.summary: The GPMP frame is explicitly defined with the computed Khufu center assigned N100000/E500000, published control-marker coordinates exist, and SP4 near the Khafre Valley Temple is published at E500390.022/N99459.759. Public Dash survey assets identify Khafre corner/center and GPMP-control datasets for acquisition.
entries.why_interesting: These resources can convert Registration Lab from model-relative controls into an externally surveyed control network once the assets are cached, hashed, parsed and transformed with residuals.
controls: keep native GPMP coordinates until transform receipt
Khafre corner estimates preserve Petrie provenance
entries.next_test: Acquire Giza-Corner-Points-2v17.kmz, GPMP-Control-Monuments.kmz and the Petrie-station table; reconcile frame metadata and solve a survey-to-Khafre local horizontal transform with holdout.
entries.guard: Published frame/control availability is not equivalent to a solved Khafre-local transform.

entries.title: Independent institutional/archaeological sources converge on the Khafre lower-complex sequence
entries.summary: Egyptian Ministry and AERA/ARCE sequence/geology sources independently point toward the Valley Temple preceding the Sphinx Temple and Sphinx-quarry phase within a Khafre-period program.
entries.why_interesting: This provides a constrained relative-construction sequence that future 3-D reconstruction should respect instead of treating lower-complex monuments as simultaneous ideal geometry.
entries.next_test: Bind ARCE 1:100 temple maps and geological block/strata records to the spatial graph with item-level provenance.
entries.guard: Strong archaeological convergence is not an absolute date or metric survey transform.

entries.title: Historical Khafre plates can be linked to modern registered imagery as a long-baseline condition record
entries.summary: Belzoni/Perring-era sections and condition descriptions now coexist with rights-reviewed modern photos and survey-control infrastructure.
entries.why_interesting: Once common features are registered, the corpus can test whether visible conditions changed over decades/centuries rather than relying on anecdotal comparison.
entries.next_test: Acquire Perring plate bytes/IIIF legally, mark shared visible features, and quantify registration residuals against survey-constrained geometry.
entries.guard: Historical drawings are not photographs or modern survey geometry.

entries.title: The confirmed corpus supports sophisticated engineering but does not currently require exotic or AI-era technology
entries.summary: Across survey, archaeology, materials, geology, imagery, chronology and museum records, no direct artifact or measurement currently establishes AI, digital computation, power machinery or other modern-equivalent technology at Giza.
entries.why_interesting: This defines a falsifiable baseline: future extraordinary-technology hypotheses must contribute new independently verifiable evidence beyond precision, scale or geometric regularity.
entries.next_test: Continue harvesting primary excavation/survey datasets and register actual tool-mark/material evidence before revisiting technology claims.
entries.guard: Absence of current evidence is not proof of impossibility; it is the present evidence state.

entries.title: The ARCE Sphinx archive exposes an explicit local grid and approximate vertical bridge to MSL
entries.summary: ARCE/Open Context project documentation records the Sphinx local N3000/E500 grid, its 1978 magnetic-north orientation, a +10 m local elevation marker, and an approximate +9.331 m conversion from Sphinx local elevations to mean sea level according to the project tie.
entries.why_interesting: This is a concrete published datum definition that may eventually help reconcile Sphinx/Valley Temple mapping with GPMP and Khafre control, but only after independent frame/datum checks.
controls: do not apply +9.331 m to Khafre automatically
require common control points and residuals
entries.next_test: Acquire/hash the Open Context project JSON and relevant map/control records, then solve an explicit ARCE-Sphinx→GPMP transform with independent holdouts.
entries.guard: The documented Sphinx datum relation is not automatically a Khafre pyramid vertical tie.

entries.title: Primary-source bytes are now the main remaining provenance gap between verified web facts and reproducible extraction
entries.summary: GIZA has a large verified source corpus, but reproducible datum extraction requires byte-level custody: exact source file, checksum, locator, parser version and output receipt. The chat sandbox cannot currently fetch those binaries directly.
entries.why_interesting: Closing this gap makes future measurements independently reproducible and prevents a later model from silently extracting from a changed webpage, different scan, or unlicensed copy.
controls: remote verification is not local possession
entries.next_test: Run the vault fetcher on a networked desktop for Petrie, Open Context and other rights-cleared assets, verify checksums, then issue first parser receipts.
entries.guard: A remote source lock or normalized snapshot is not raw source bytes and cannot be represented as such.

entries.title: Royal mortuary transition and continuing cult are the strongest current intent models
entries.summary: Current corpus independently supports burial architecture, royal funeral/afterlife function, and post-burial offering cult as central purposes of Old Kingdom pyramid complexes; these explain more observed architecture than machine or future-message hypotheses.
entries.why_interesting: This provides a falsifiable baseline intent model against which more exotic explanations must add explanatory power rather than merely fit selected geometry.
entries.next_test: Bind room-level Khafre excavation finds and processional constraints to the intent graph and test component-by-component predictions.
entries.guard: A strong mortuary/cult baseline does not imply every architectural or symbolic feature is fully understood.

entries.title: A distant-future encoded message remains unestablished
entries.summary: Precision, durability and symbolic monumentality are compatible with long-lived communication, but the current corpus contains no explicit future-audience marker or independently decodable technical payload.
entries.why_interesting: The question can be tested rigorously once survey-grade geometry is available by preregistering encoding hypotheses and using cross-monument holdouts and multiple-comparisons controls.
entries.next_test: After survey-frame reconciliation, run a blinded cross-monument encoding test that forbids post-hoc ratio selection.
entries.guard: Do not infer intended future communication from numerical coincidence or monument durability alone.

entries.title: Khafre Valley Temple concentrated repeated royal-image evidence at the lower complex
entries.summary: Digital Giza catalogs multiple Khafre statues/fragments from the Valley Temple, while the Egyptian Museum records a 168 cm diorite Khafre statue from the temple and describes it as one of about 23 similar statues.
entries.why_interesting: This makes encounter with royal imagery a stronger action-graph constraint than a generic symbolic guess, even though exact ancient positions remain unresolved.
controls: separate find provenance from original placement
no ritual action inferred solely from iconography
entries.next_test: Acquire rights-cleared valley-temple plans/excavation records and map statue bases/findspots to exact rooms and sightlines.
entries.guard: Repeated statuary establishes royal-image presence, not the exact ceremony performed around it.

entries.title: The complex supports a constrained place/action sequence but not a recovered ritual script
entries.summary: Valley Temple, causeway, pyramid-temple court, burial architecture and post-burial cult function can be linked into a source-addressed behavioral graph, but exact actors, spoken rites, timing and room-level choreography remain only partially constrained.
entries.why_interesting: This converts the “what were they doing?” question into explicit missing measurements and source targets instead of unconstrained narrative.
controls: every action node requires source-addressed evidence
direct architecture separated from inferred behavior
no score interpreted as historical probability
entries.next_test: Parse Hölscher/Petrie/Perring plans and excavation locators to replace component-level nodes with room/threshold-level action constraints.
entries.guard: Graph connectivity is a research model, not ancient testimony.

entries.title: Khafre lower-to-upper route contains repeated architectural thresholding
entries.summary: Room-level reconstruction now exposes repeated transitions—dual lower entrances, vestibule/hall transitions, causeway termination/branching, pillared halls, court, inner cult spaces, and burial passage controls. This is a topological pattern to test, not proof of a scripted initiation sequence.
entries.null_or_control: Compare threshold density and access hierarchy with contemporaneous Old Kingdom royal complexes once equivalent room graphs are built.
entries.why_interesting: Repeated thresholding may encode functional hierarchy, circulation control, or ritual staging. The pattern is testable against peer Old Kingdom complexes rather than being accepted as symbolic by inspection.
entries.next_test: Build equivalent room graphs for Khufu/Menkaure and register metric Khafre plans; compare threshold density, branching, route depth and access centrality under matched definitions.
entries.guard: Topological pattern only. Repeated thresholds do not prove an initiation sequence, secret message, or specific ritual script.

entries.title: Royal imagery appears spatially integrated with circulation rather than merely collected
entries.summary: Valley Temple niche fields and Pyramid Temple court emplacement evidence make royal statuary part of the movement environment. Exact original placements remain partly reconstructed.
entries.null_or_control: Compare with statue placement/circulation in other Fourth–Fifth Dynasty pyramid complexes and preserve findspot-vs-original-placement distinctions.
entries.why_interesting: If royal images were repeatedly positioned along architectural movement states, imagery may have structured experience rather than functioning as an undifferentiated statue collection.
entries.next_test: Acquire plan/source bytes for Valley Temple and Pyramid Temple, map only securely anchored installation traces, and compare circulation-relative placement across peer royal complexes.
entries.guard: Presence and installation traces are evidence; exact statue identities, original positions, viewing order and ritual meaning remain partly reconstructed.

entries.title: Primary plan bytes are now the bottleneck for room-level reconstruction
entries.summary: The archive inventory proves that room-scale drawings exist, including a 1:100 Khafre Valley Temple map, but this runtime still lacks checksum-bound plan bytes. The next promotion bottleneck is source custody and metric registration, not more narrative inference.
entries.null_or_control: Acquire/hash plan bytes, parse with independent holdouts, and compare against historical plans before geometry promotion.
entries.why_interesting: Room-level interpretation has reached the limit of schematic topology. The highest-value uncertainty reduction now comes from exact primary plan custody and registration rather than additional narrative detail.
entries.next_test: Acquire legal/open plan bytes, hash them, parse native scale/frame, register independent controls and holdouts, then compare extracted room polygons against at least one independent historical or modern plan.
entries.guard: Plan availability, OCR and published scale metadata do not authorize metric geometry or zero uncertainty.

entries.title: Khafre plan evidence separates into convergent architecture and disputed reconstruction
entries.summary: Independent source families converge on the Valley Temple dual-entry/T-hall program, 23 statuary positions, covered causeway, Pyramid Temple hall/court/five-chapel program, and core pyramid-interior topology, while court statue form/placement and some cult-room contents remain explicitly disputed or interpretive.
entries.why_interesting: GIZA can now use agreement structure rather than a single preferred reconstruction, reducing the risk of baking one scholar’s restoration into the model.
controls: no plan catalog record treated as parsed metric geometry
entries.next_test: Acquire/hash source plan bytes, parse scales and wall polygons, then measure residual agreement between independently registered plans.
entries.guard: Cross-source agreement increases confidence in topology, not automatic geometry authority.

entries.title: The documented route crosses repeated changes in spatial/visual environment
entries.summary: The source-backed topology moves through exterior thresholds, a pillar-and-royal-image hall, a covered linear ascent, a branching upper entrance, pillared halls/court, inner rooms, physical closure and an enclosed burial endpoint. This creates a testable sequence of environmental state changes.
entries.why_interesting: If metric plans and heights later confirm strong visual/illumination/access contrasts at the same thresholds, GIZA can test whether the sequence is architecturally staged rather than merely connected.
controls: no ritual inference from contrast alone
holdout against other Old Kingdom complexes
entries.next_test: Register legal plan bytes and compute actual line-of-sight/occlusion, sky visibility and route-choice metrics with uncertainty envelopes.
entries.guard: A repeated environmental transition pattern is not proof of ceremony, symbolism, or intended emotional effect.

entries.title: A procedural architectural grammar is the strongest pre-metric pattern
entries.summary: Across independently supported room programs, the Khafre complex repeatedly transforms movement: dual entry converges, royal-image space precedes a covered linear ascent, the upper temple branches and deepens, and the pyramid interior introduces literal closure before the burial endpoint.
entries.why_interesting: This is more structurally constrained than isolated numerical coincidences and yields direct metric tests at doors, wall openings, turns, image fields and closure points.
controls: metric registration required before sightline claims
entries.next_test: Register independent Valley Temple and pyramid-interior plan sources, then test whether visibility/reveal transitions survive metric geometry and comparative controls.
entries.guard: The grammar is a design hypothesis, not an ancient script, code or evidence of advanced computation.

entries.title: Valley Temple material-image-light staging is a concrete metric test target
entries.summary: Hölscher reconstructs a Valley Temple hall combining dark granite, bright alabaster, royal statues and light entering from high openings with reflected effects. ARCE’s 1:100 mapping offers a route to test the geometry behind that reconstruction.
entries.why_interesting: It converts a vivid historical description into a falsifiable spatial question: where could light enter and which image positions could be visible from each route state?
entries.next_test: Resolve ARCE 1:100 drawing bytes and register wall/opening geometry; compare against Hölscher reconstruction without forcing a match.
entries.guard: Even a successful geometric reconstruction would establish physical plausibility, not intended symbolism or psychological effect.

entries.title: Plate-local metric visibility can precede plateau-wide georeferencing
entries.summary: A checksum-bound plan can be registered to PLATE_LOCAL_METERS and support intra-building wall/opening geometry and metric rays without first solving GPMP→Khafre global translation.
entries.why_interesting: This separates room-scale visibility from the harder plateau geodesy problem and prevents an unnecessary global-frame bottleneck.
entries.next_test: Acquire Petrie Plate VI bytes and run the frozen similarity/holdout protocol.
entries.guard: Local metric validity does not imply correct placement on the Giza plateau.

entries.title: First archaeological plate fit is now protected by preregistered holdout thresholds
entries.summary: Similarity-model choice, minimum controls/holdouts, residual normalization, outlier policy and acceptance limits are frozen before the first source-byte fit.
entries.why_interesting: This blocks post-hoc threshold selection and model escalation after seeing the archaeological residuals.
controls: model complexity cannot increase without new preregistration
entries.next_test: Run unchanged thresholds against Petrie Plate VI and report pass/fail without tuning.
entries.guard: Passing a registration validates map geometry within the declared frame; it does not prove ritual meaning.

entries.title: Petrie source identity is verified while local byte custody remains blocked by runtime transfer
entries.summary: Wikimedia Commons identifies the 315-page 8.87 MB public-domain Petrie scan and Digital Giza independently catalogs the 1883 work; two local acquisition paths failed in this execution environment, so SHA-256/local custody remains absent.
entries.why_interesting: The evidence model distinguishes source existence, licensing and catalog identity from the separate operational fact of local byte possession.
controls: no copied hash from unverified third party
entries.next_test: Run desktop acquisition script with network access and compare computed SHA-256 to a second independently downloaded copy.
entries.guard: Transfer failure is not evidence against the source and is not permission to fabricate source bytes.

entries.title: Petrie Plate VI is dimension-rich and exactly located, but original-byte custody remains blocked
entries.summary: Petrie Plate VI is now exactly located at PDF page 305 and remotely verified as the 1:200 Granite Temple plan. Petrie chapter XIV provides numerous scalar dimensions, but the original PDF bytes are not locally checksum-bound, so pixel registration remains prohibited.
entries.why_interesting: The campaign has moved from unknown plate identity to a reproducible target with source-reported dimensional constraints without crossing the byte-custody boundary.
controls: remote render grants no pixel authority
dimension graph preserves approximate and lower-bound qualifiers
no wall polygons from scalar facts alone
entries.next_test: Acquire exact PDF bytes, hash them, visually confirm page 305, freeze pixel controls/holdouts, and run the preregistered similarity fit once.
entries.guard: A remotely viewed plan and source dimensions are not equivalent to a registered metric plan.

entries.title: Khafre lower-complex geometry appears to negotiate ridge topography rather than obey a perfect abstract grid
entries.summary: Petrie reports that the causeway is not due east/square to the temple-pyramid system and attributes the divergence to the ridge topography; he further interprets the lower entrance passage as adjusted to meet that route.
entries.why_interesting: This makes landscape constraint a testable design variable and weakens simplistic perfect-grid narratives while strengthening integrated architecture-plus-geology models.
controls: separate observed misalignment from Petrie causal interpretation
do not infer symbolism from misalignment alone
entries.next_test: Register modern and historical lower-complex plans and compare causeway/entrance axes against mapped ridge and quarry topography.
entries.guard: Observed/sketched misalignment does not by itself establish why the ancient builders chose the route.

entries.title: Petrie description makes controlled light/visibility contrast a falsifiable architectural hypothesis
entries.summary: Petrie describes long internal vistas, reflected roof light and a bright extended causeway in his reconstruction of the Granite Temple environment. Combined with the constrained movement graph, this motivates a future metric visibility/light test.
entries.why_interesting: The sensory hypothesis can eventually be tested against registered apertures, wall geometry and solar bounds instead of being treated as atmosphere or symbolism.
controls: Petrie reconstruction is not measured photometry
entries.next_test: After plate registration, digitize only evidence-supported openings/walls and compute visibility first; defer lighting simulation until heights/apertures are bounded.
entries.guard: Physical visibility or illumination plausibility does not prove ritual intent.

entries.title: First-plate landmark classes are fixed before archaeological pixel coordinates exist
entries.summary: Ten named Plate VI landmark classes are distributed across five architectural sectors while every pixel and metric coordinate remains null until a checksum-bound local render exists.
entries.why_interesting: This removes another researcher degree of freedom: candidate correspondence types are chosen before residuals can influence which features are selected.
controls: controls span at least three sectors
holdouts span at least two sectors
entries.next_test: Populate the preregistered landmarks against a checksum-bound Plate VI render and freeze roles before the first archaeological solve.
entries.guard: Preregistering landmark classes improves falsifiability; it does not make the historical plan accurate or metric by itself.
